reasoning: A graph with girth at least 8 cannot have any vertex of degree 3 or higher on only 16 vertices, because the Moore lower bound on the number of vertices for degree d=3 and girth g=8 is 1 + 3 + 6 + 12 = 22 (ball of radius 3 around a degree-3 vertex unfolds as a tree without cycles of length <8). However, a graph with 16 vertices and at least 21 edges must have average degree at least 2.625, hence at least one vertex of degree >=3 by the handshaking lemma. This is a contradiction, so no such graph exists (it is also 3-colorable only if it exists, but it cannot).
